dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The brain dump plus answers define a concrete goal: a personal home-lab image wall showing recent posts from a curated set of one seed profile's Following, served to a website UI through a reusable FFI library, built conservatively to protect a real cookie-jar account.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Seven measurable goals are stated, each with an observable change (FFI-callable, zero friendship-endpoint calls on normal runs, off-by-default harvest, carousel/video flags, panic-safe boundary, a library-enforced pacing floor, and the CLI exit-code contract preserved).

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Ten pass/fail criteria, each carrying a runnable check: cargo build/test, an offline FFI smoke that never touches live Instagram, a lexical guard isolating the friendship endpoint to one file, panic-safety and exit-code tests, a pacing-floor test, and cargo fmt --check + clippy.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: Explicit in-scope, out-of-scope, and future lists were locked across five interview decisions and refined by the plan critics (consumer-side cache, library-side pacing floor, hand-written header at MVP).

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: The conservative-cookie-jar vs fan-out tension is resolved inside the library: a cached list plus a rare opt-in harvest keep normal runs off the friendship endpoint, and a Session-enforced minimum inter-scrape pacing floor means account safety does not depend on the out-of-scope caller's loop.

problem: instagrab today is a one-shot CLI that scrapes a flat list of Instagram usernames and writes JSONL. The user is building a separate website UI (any language, on their home lab) that needs to show a wall of recent images from the people one seed profile follows — and it needs to drive the scraper on demand, per friend, not just read a nightly file. The current binary can't be called from another process, only run.

Two capabilities are missing outright. First, the code reads only follower/following counts, never the actual member list, so there is no way to discover who to fan out over. Second, that member list can only come from Instagram's private friendship endpoints, which 2025-26 enforcement treats as a top ban trigger — and the whole project's design ethos is to protect a real logged-in account. The design must add friends-list discovery and per-friend fan-out without turning normal runs into the exact request pattern that gets accounts suspended, and without letting account safety depend on an out-of-scope caller pacing its own loop.
goals: Expose instagrab as a C-ABI library so a web service in any language can drive it over FFI: a caller can connect, scrape one username, receive valid JSON, free it, and disconnect without crashing.

A normal fan-out run makes zero calls to the friendship endpoints — only web_profile_info and the post feed — producing one JSON result per reachable friend with posts limited to the rolling last-N-days window.
Provide friends-list discovery as a separate, off-by-default harvest call that pages the seed's Following once at human pace and returns the usernames; persisting them is the consumer's job.
Flag carousels and videos in each post's output (media_count, has_video) so the UI can badge a post and link out to Instagram, while only the first image is downloaded.
Make the FFI boundary panic-safe: any error crosses as an error JSON payload, never as a process-aborting panic.
Enforce a minimum inter-scrape pacing floor inside the library so a naive caller loop cannot exceed a safe request rate — account safety lives in the brain, not the caller.
Preserve the existing CLI's cron behavior and exit-code contract (0 OK, 1 config, 2 logged_out, 3 schema_drift, 4 browser, 5 canary_failed), now built on top of the library.

mvp.item: Post output gains media_count / is_carousel / has_video flags; first image still the only download
mvp.reason: Directly serves the 'tell me if there's more, I'll go to IG' decision and is a small additive parser change

mvp.item: src/harvest.rs: a dedicated module that pages the seed's Following once via the attached Chrome, parses the friendship page, and returns the usernames — the ONLY file referencing the friendship endpoint
mvp.reason: The only sanctioned-by-design way to discover the fan-out set (goal #3), quarantined so the ban-trigger code is a single-file lexical guard

mvp.item: Consumer-side cache: harvest returns the list; the CLI persists it to a file and its fan-out mode reads it back (the library stays stateless between calls)
mvp.reason: Gives the cache a named reader while honoring decision #5 — persistence is a consumer concern, not library state

mvp.item: CLI gains a fan-out mode that reads the cached friends list instead of config.usernames
mvp.reason: Makes the CLI a real consumer of the cache and the home-lab cron path for the fan-out

mvp.item: Session enforces a minimum inter-scrape pacing floor (safe default, configurable)
mvp.reason: Account safety must not depend on the out-of-scope website pacing its own loop; the floor keeps a naive caller under a safe rate

mvp.item: Public Rust library API (Session connect / harvest / scrape_one / disconnect) extracted from main.rs, with an explicit idle timeout and reconnectable dropped-connection errors
mvp.reason: The library is the whole point; the FFI layer wraps it, and caller-driven gaps between calls can be unbounded

mvp.item: C-ABI FFI layer: extern "C" over an opaque handle, JSON in/out, catch_unwind, free_string, and a hand-written checked-in C header (include/instagrab.h)
mvp.reason: Goal #1 — callable from any language; a hand-written header is the minimum-viable artifact for ~6 functions

mvp.item: CLI rewritten as a thin consumer of the library, preserving exit codes + JSONL + canary + jitter
scripts/ffi-smoke: a non-Rust caller exercising the FFI lifecycle offline (no live Instagram)
mvp.reason: Proves goal #1 mechanically without spending cookie-jar risk on every verification

decisions.decision: Discover friends via a cached list on disk, (re)built by a rare, explicit, off-by-default harvest
decisions.rejected: Auto-fetching the Following list on every run (or hand-typing usernames only)
decisions.reason: Instagram's friendship endpoints are the top ban trigger under 2025-26 enforcement; the followers dialog is just a UI over the same endpoint, so safety comes from rarity and human pacing, not from DOM-vs-endpoint. A cached list keeps normal runs off the endpoint entirely.

decisions.decision: Ship instagrab as a C-ABI FFI library callable from any language
decisions.rejected: A Rust-only web service, or a long-running HTTP daemon
decisions.reason: The user wants to FFI into the brain from a web service written in any language, keeping the site's language independent of Rust.

decisions.decision: Download only the first image per post, but flag carousels and videos in the output
decisions.rejected: Downloading every carousel image and/or the video files
decisions.reason: The user prefers to open Instagram directly for the full set; flagging keeps storage and bandwidth on the home lab small.

decisions.decision: Apply a rolling last-N-days window per friend, reusing the existing time_window_days
decisions.rejected: A fixed [start, end] date range, or latest-page-only with no time filter
decisions.reason: Matches the user's 'images for a set of time' and is already implemented per-profile in parse.rs.

decisions.decision: Expose granular, caller-driven FFI calls as the primary surface; the library stays stateless between calls and the caller owns the loop and resume
decisions.rejected: A single batch call as the primary surface (a convenience batch call is deferred to future, not permanently rejected)
decisions.reason: Granular calls give the UI per-friend progress and survive restarts, and they push fan-out loop state into the web service where it belongs.

decisions.decision: Enforce a minimum inter-scrape pacing floor inside the library (Session-level)
decisions.rejected: Relying on the existing CLI jitter or on the out-of-scope caller to pace its own loop
decisions.reason: Critic fix (hidden-dependency blocker): the existing jitter lives only in the CLI loop, but decision #5 hands the loop to the out-of-scope website — a naive UI loop would hammer IG at full speed. Putting the floor in the library keeps account safety in the brain regardless of caller behavior.

decisions.decision: Isolate the friendship-endpoint fetch in a dedicated src/harvest.rs module
decisions.rejected: Adding harvest_following alongside the feed fetch in src/scraper.rs
decisions.reason: Critic fix (success-criteria blocker): quarantining the endpoint literal to one file makes the 'normal runs never touch the friendship endpoint' guarantee a single-file lexical check (grep -rl), which a shared module could not provide.

decisions.decision: Keep all contract verification offline; the live FFI smoke against Instagram is a manual, deliberate dev step
decisions.rejected: Making a live canary scrape a top-level pass/fail success criterion
decisions.reason: Critic fix (hidden-dependency + scope-creep blockers): CLAUDE.md forbids integration tests against live IG because every run costs cookie-jar risk; an offline lifecycle smoke proves the FFI boundary without spending that risk on every verification.

phases.title: Capabilities: media flags, harvest, cache
phases.notes: Additive within the current architecture. parse.rs gains media_count/is_carousel/has_video. A NEW src/harvest.rs is the only file that references the friendship endpoint: it fetches and parses the seed's Following page and returns the usernames (no live-IG test — fixture-driven). A consumer-side cache helper writes/reads the friends list. All fixture-testable via cargo test.

phases.title: Library extraction
phases.notes: Create lib.rs exposing a Rust API (Session::connect / harvest / scrape_one / disconnect) with typed results and no process::exit. Session::connect takes or derives an explicit CDP idle timeout, and scrape_one on a dropped connection maps to a machine-readable, reconnectable error (caller-driven gaps between calls are unbounded). The Session enforces the minimum inter-scrape pacing floor. Split the crate into lib + bin; rewrite main.rs as a thin consumer preserving exit codes, JSONL, canary, jitter, and add the CLI fan-out mode that reads the cache.

phases.title: C-ABI FFI + build
phases.notes: Add ffi.rs: extern "C" functions over an opaque session handle, JSON marshaling, catch_unwind, free_string. Set Cargo crate-type to include cdylib. Hand-write and check in include/instagrab.h (cbindgen automation is deferred to Full). Add scripts/ffi-smoke (offline lifecycle, no live IG). The deploy target is a Linux x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu .so — spell out the concrete scripts/release change to emit it (the current static-musl pipeline copies only the binary and cannot emit a loadable library).
